dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: June 26: SpaceX Pursues Dedicated Natural Gas Pipeline to Meet Starship Propellant Demands
heroSubtitle: 8,798 days since SpaceX founding — On June 7, 2026 at 04:24 UTC, SpaceX launched its 71st orbital mission of the year from Vandenberg SLC-4E, carrying 21 Starlink V2 Mini Optimized satellites and 2 Starshield (government-variant) satellites; the Falcon 9 first stage landed on drone ship OCISLY in the Pacific — the 622nd cumulative SpaceX booster recovery. The co-manifest of Starshield on a commercial Starlink launch represents a rare public acknowledgment of the classified government satellite program. The launch occurred as SpaceX's IPO roadshow entered day 4: Reuters reported June 6 that SpaceX is signaling confidence at the fixed $135/share offer price, with investor demand surging and private secondary markets trading $129–$137. Approximately 125 analysts from 21 underwriting banks covered the roadshow; IPO pricing is set for June 11 and the Nasdaq (SPCX) debut for June 12. The implied valuation of $1.77T (~$75B raise on 555.56M Class A shares) would be the largest IPO in history. Meanwhile, Starship remains FAA-grounded pending IFT-12 mishap investigation — IFT-13 (Booster 20 + Ship 40) targets July–August 2026.
